paragraphs: The 420i has been a core entry-level petrol model in the 4 Series range since its launch in 2013, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F32-generation cars (2013 to 2016) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine that was BMW's first mass-market turbo-four. From 2016, the F32-generation 420i switched to the B48, a newer 2.0-litre turbo-four that's a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the N20. The current G22-generation 420i (2020–present) continues with a further-evolved B48. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the known wear pattern differs between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 420i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the early F32-generation 420i. Known for timing chain guide failure over time — see the callout above. We replace timing chains, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

The current 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine, fitted from the 2016 F32 facelift onward and continuing into the G22 generation. The B48 is generally considered significantly more reliable than the N20, with no comparable well-documented timing chain pattern.

compatibility.intro: Because the 420i spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 420i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
